ideas.title: The Charter
ideas.note: earn a civic building once (Records Hall, Mint, Almshouse) and it stands in *every* future town — The fleet called this the strongest single idea it produced. It's the thing that makes days accumulate into something instead of resetting. v4 already lands the `extraSites` hook it needs, so it starts warm.

ideas.title: Coverage sentinel: the tracker notices untracked AI usage instead of the user noticing it
ideas.note: Watch for signs of harness activity that produced no usage events (e.g. codex.exe/claude processes running, or known AI dirs like ~/.codex being written) and show a "possible untracked usage" warning with what ran and when. Strongest signal: the provider-side rate-limit windows the tracker already polls (CodexLimitsService/ClaudeLimitsService) are billing-side truth that count even trace-less calls — if a window's used% climbs while the local ledger stays flat, something ran untracked. Every miss so far was found by the user eyeballing dashboards; this flips detection to the tracker.

ideas.title: Per-file client sniff fallback: a codex-shaped file in a claude-tagged root is silently ignored
ideas.note: Roots carry one client tag, and every *.jsonl under them is parsed with that client's parser only (loop-learning\data\runs is claude-tagged, so codex-shaped files there yield zero events, no error). When a file produces no events under its root's parser, re-sniff it and parse with the shape it actually matches.

ideas.title: Keep a history of the plan-limit meters, not just the latest reading
ideas.note: The Limits page polls the 5h / Week / Fable percentages every few minutes but only the latest snapshot survives (accounts.json). Append every distinct reading (account, label, percent, resetsAt, fetchedMs) to a small limit_readings table in usage.db and prune after ~90 days. With that, 'did Anthropic shrink the 5h window?' is one query: tokens spent between two readings divided by the percent moved, plotted over weeks. On 2026-09-04 answering it took an hour of forensics across transcript error lines and bot chat logs, and July was unanswerable.

ideas.title: Attribute a session to the account it started under, not the one signed in now
ideas.note: A running Claude Code process keeps the OAuth token it read at launch, so when claude-swap switches accounts the bot's long-lived sessions keep charging the old account for hours. The Limits page's local-usage-per-account attribution uses the signed-in timeline at each event's time, so those events land on the wrong account (seen 2026-09-04: account A's 5h meter rose 17->25% while the timeline attributed $0 to it; account B's readings matched only after re-attributing by session start). Fix: attribute each top-level session (and its subagents) to the account active at its first event; a session that outlives a swap stays with its original account.

ideas.title: Keep a copy of transcripts that vanish seconds after they're indexed, so Live blocks always open
ideas.note: Cause: the Discord bot's narrator forks (`claude -p --resume --fork-session`), refusal-rewind cuts and model-restore copies each write a new full-history .jsonl under ~/.claude/projects, the tracker indexes it within a second, and the bot unlinks it right after (narrator.js:723, bot.js:10021/10087/10237/10554/20850). In the last 3 days 2,656 of 7,698 Claude events (380 files, all from the bot's agents) point at deleted files, so double-clicking those blocks shows "The log this block came from is gone". Fix in the tracker: tee the complete lines the parser already reads into a compressed vault under the data dir keyed by source path; drop a vault copy once its source has survived ~24h (so the vault only ends up holding files that actually disappeared), cap the vault by size/age; the transcript viewer falls back to the vault when the recorded path is missing. Alternative, cheaper but outside this repo: have the bot move those copies to an archive folder instead of unlinking.
ideas.result: The collector tees every young transcript it parses into %LOCALAPPDATA%\TokenTracker\transcript-vault; copies whose source survives a day are dropped, copies of vanished logs are gzipped and kept (30 days / 1 GB, settings.json). Double-clicking a block whose log was deleted now opens the copy and says so in the header. Verified live: a bot fork vanished, was compressed 234 KB to 68 KB and stayed openable.

ideas.title: Count Codex runs that save no transcript (codex exec --ephemeral)
ideas.note:
Why: --ephemeral writes no rollout to ~/.codex/sessions, and the rollout was the tracker's only Codex source. It kept recurring: loop-learning lost ~150 calls on 2026-08-27 and built its own mirror (tools/model_backend.mjs); machinelearning/tinyboss/gen.mjs ran an ~800-call GPT-6 Luna job on 2026-09-24 that was never counted.

Built with Codex's rollout tracer instead of a relay: Codex 0.156 ignores OPENAI_BASE_URL for ChatGPT logins, and --ignore-user-config drops openai_base_url. The app sets the user-level CODEX_ROLLOUT_TRACE_ROOT to its data folder (cleared on exit); every Codex process writes a trace bundle there with each call's token_usage, even with --ephemeral --ignore-user-config. Only threads with no rollout path are billed, so nothing counts twice; bundles are pruned once indexed. loop-learning's mirror now stands down while the trace root is set.
ideas.result: Settings → Count Codex runs that save no session log (on by default); covers Codex processes started after the app sets the variable.
